title: AID Protocol v2 — Waiver
$comment: producer: C4/PM, consumers: [FSM, release_decision, PM brief, GUI]
description: Artifact recording an explicit, visible waiver of a release blocker. A waiver is a governance record — never an empty rubber-stamp — so its reason must be substantive (>= 20 chars) and it is always visible.

allOf.$comment: extends aid-protocol-v2.schema.json envelope (reference only — not a resolved $ref)

waiver.$comment: enforced — reason minLength (>= 20) is validated by aid-protocol-validate.sh (exit 17); payload-key presence is validated by step 12 (exit 12).

waived_check.description: Identifier of the check/blocker being waived.

waived_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp with Z suffix.

visible.description: A waiver is always visible — it can never be hidden from the PM surface.

forced_override.description: True when this waiver records a PM --force bypass rather than an ordinary release-blocker waiver. Optional: an ordinary waiver omits it.
forced_override.$comment: P073 Step 7 — declared here so the field is documented and validated; it is a TOP-LEVEL artifact field because `additionalProperties: false` applies to the `waiver` subobject only.

bypassed_preconditions.description: Names of the forceable preconditions this force bypassed, in the order they failed. Present only on a force waiver, and never empty — a force that bypassed nothing writes no waiver at all.
bypassed_preconditions.$comment: P073 Step 7 — top-level for the same reason as forced_override.

candidate_sha.description: The frozen plan-final candidate this force was recorded against, when one exists.
candidate_sha.$comment: P073 Step 7 — optional; null before a freeze.
